lily-greeting.text: Hello again! I am planning a welcome day for new visitors. Could you help me make a thoughtful plan?

welcome-0-say.text: Welcome to Little Harbor! We are planning a welcome day for new visitors. Introduce yourself with an explorer name, and tell me something you enjoy.

welcome-0-hint.text: My explorer name is Sunny, and I enjoy learning about animals.

welcome-0-feedback.text: Lovely to meet you! Your interests will help us choose a good first stop.

welcome-1-say.text: We can start at the library or the fish market. Which place would you choose, and why? Give me a reason, not just the name.

welcome-1-hint.text: I would choose the library because I enjoy reading animal stories.

welcome-1-feedback.text: That sounds like a thoughtful choice. A reason helps other people understand your plan.

welcome-2-say.text: Please check the sign outside the library. When does it open, and when does it close? Tell me both times in one sentence.

welcome-2-hint.text: The library opens at nine and closes at five.

welcome-2-feedback.text: Exactly. We can visit during the afternoon and still have plenty of time.

welcome-3-say.text: A visitor is standing at the library and wants to reach the fish market. The fountain is between them. Give directions using past and then.

welcome-3-hint.text: Walk past the fountain, and then continue east to the fish market.

welcome-3-feedback.text: Clear directions! Mentioning a landmark makes a route easier to follow.

welcome-4-say.text: Let's invite Mia to meet us in the town square at three o'clock. Make the invitation friendly, and remember the place and the time.

welcome-4-hint.text: Would you like to meet us in the town square at three o'clock?

welcome-4-feedback.text: That is a friendly invitation. Mia will know exactly where and when to meet us.

welcome-5-say.text: Oh dear, the forecast says it may rain. The library has room indoors. Suggest a change to our plan and explain why it would help.

welcome-5-hint.text: We could meet inside the library because it will keep everyone dry.

welcome-5-feedback.text: Good thinking. Changing a plan can help everyone stay comfortable.

welcome-6-say.text: Now give our visitors a short plan. Use first and then, name two places, and finish by reminding them to meet us at three.

welcome-6-hint.text: First we will visit the library, then the fish market, and meet at three.

welcome-6-feedback.text: Our welcome-day plan is ready. You introduced yourself, gave directions, and solved a problem. Thank you!

mia-greeting.text: Welcome to the fish market! Today we are helping a customer compare prices and choose fish within a budget.

market-0-say.text: A customer needs help choosing fish for a make-believe aquarium. They have one hundred and ten coins. Offer to help them, using a polite full sentence.

market-0-hint.text: I would be happy to help you choose some fish today.

market-0-feedback.text: Thank you. Let's compare the choices before we make a recommendation.

market-1-say.text: Read the price board beside my market. Which is cheaper, the goldfish or the blue tang? Explain your answer using both prices.

market-1-hint.text: The goldfish is cheaper because it costs forty-five coins, not sixty.

market-1-feedback.text: Correct. The goldfish costs fifteen coins less than the blue tang.

market-2-say.text: The customer likes a guppy for fifty coins and a blue tang for sixty. How much would they spend altogether, and would their budget be enough?

market-2-hint.text: They would spend one hundred and ten coins, so their budget is enough.

market-2-feedback.text: Exactly. The two fish use the whole budget, so there would be no coins left.

market-3-say.text: The customer's aquarium has room for only two more fish. Should they buy three small fish or the pair we discussed? Explain your choice.

market-3-hint.text: They should buy the pair because there is only room for two fish.

market-3-feedback.text: Yes. Checking the available space is just as important as checking the price.

market-4-say.text: The customer also asks where tall plants should go. Suggest a place that leaves open water for swimming, and give a reason.

market-4-hint.text: Put the tall plants at the back so the fish have space to swim.

market-4-feedback.text: That layout keeps a clear swimming area and makes the aquarium easy to see.

market-5-say.text: You are not sure whether a decoration costs thirty or forty coins. Ask me to check the price. Use a polite question instead of guessing.

market-5-hint.text: Could you please tell me how much this decoration costs?

market-5-feedback.text: Of course. Asking for clarification is a useful skill whenever you are shopping.

market-6-say.text: Tell me the customer's final order: a guppy and a blue tang. Include please and the total price in a complete sentence.

market-6-hint.text: We would like a guppy and a blue tang, please, for one hundred and ten coins.

market-6-feedback.text: The shopping plan is complete. You compared prices, checked space, and placed a clear order. Well done!

ben-greeting.text: Hello, designer! I have a new aquarium design brief. We need a beautiful layout and a sensible budget.

design-0-say.text: A visitor wants an aquarium that feels peaceful. Describe the kind of aquarium you would design. Include at least one detail about its colors or decorations.

design-0-hint.text: I would design a peaceful aquarium with green plants and smooth stones.

design-0-feedback.text: That gives us a useful starting point. Now let's work out what we can afford.

design-1-say.text: Look at the design board beside my workshop. A pebble arch costs fifty coins and seaweed costs thirty-five. Tell me the cost of both together.

design-1-hint.text: The pebble arch and the seaweed cost eighty-five coins altogether.

design-1-feedback.text: Yes, eighty-five coins altogether. We should always add the prices before buying.

design-2-say.text: Our customer has one hundred coins. After spending eighty-five, how much will be left? Explain the subtraction in a sentence.

design-2-hint.text: After spending eighty-five coins, the customer will have fifteen coins left.

design-2-feedback.text: Correct. Saving the remaining coins could help with a future aquarium upgrade.

design-3-say.text: Now describe where the two decorations should go. Put the seaweed at the back and choose a position for the arch. Use two location phrases.

design-3-hint.text: The seaweed goes at the back, and the arch goes in the middle.

design-3-feedback.text: I can picture your layout. Location words make your instructions much clearer.

design-4-say.text: Why did you leave the middle of the aquarium fairly open? Explain how that choice helps the fish or helps us see them.

design-4-hint.text: I left some open space because the fish need room to swim around.

design-4-feedback.text: Exactly. A useful design considers the living space as well as the decorations.

design-5-say.text: Imagine that the arch is difficult to move. Ask me for help with moving it. Be specific, and make your request polite.

design-5-hint.text: Could you please help me move the arch a little to the left?

design-5-feedback.text: Of course. A specific request tells the other person what help you need.

design-6-say.text: Give the customer your final recommendation. Name both decorations, explain where the seaweed goes, and say how much the plan costs.

design-6-hint.text: Choose the arch and seaweed, put the seaweed at the back, and spend eighty-five coins.

design-6-feedback.text: Your design brief is complete. You planned the cost, described a layout, and explained your choices. Beautiful work!

finn-greeting.text: Ahoy, explorer! A boat is waiting for a delivery. Let's check the schedule, count the boxes, and keep an eye on the weather.

delivery-0-say.text: Ahoy! We have a delivery to organize before a boat leaves the harbor. Offer to help, and tell me one job you could do.

delivery-0-hint.text: I can help with the delivery by counting the boxes for you.

delivery-0-feedback.text: Excellent. Let's read the schedule carefully before we start moving anything.

delivery-1-say.text: Check the notice beside the harbor gate. Which pier is the delivery going to, and what time does the boat leave? Include both details.

delivery-1-hint.text: The delivery goes to East Pier, and the boat leaves at four thirty.

delivery-1-feedback.text: That's right: East Pier, at four thirty. Clear details prevent a lot of confusion.

delivery-2-say.text: There are three red boxes and two blue boxes. Tell me how many boxes we have altogether, using a complete sentence.

delivery-2-hint.text: There are five boxes altogether, with three red boxes and two blue boxes.

delivery-2-feedback.text: Five boxes. Now we can check that every box arrives at the right place.

delivery-3-say.text: It is four o'clock now, and the boat leaves at four thirty. How much time do we have left? Tell me what we should do next.

delivery-3-hint.text: We have thirty minutes left, so we should move the boxes to East Pier.

delivery-3-feedback.text: Good planning. We have enough time if we stay organized and work carefully.

delivery-4-say.text: We need a rope, and Ben has one at his workshop. What would you say to ask if you may borrow it? Include the reason you need it.

delivery-4-hint.text: Could I please borrow a rope because we need it for the delivery?

delivery-4-feedback.text: That request is polite and clear. Giving a reason helps Ben understand the situation.

delivery-5-say.text: The wind has become stronger. Read the notice at the lighthouse lookout. Should we leave immediately, or wait? Explain what the sign tells us to do.

delivery-5-hint.text: We should wait in the harbor until the light turns green because of the wind.

delivery-5-feedback.text: Exactly. We wait for the green signal. A schedule is important, but safe decisions come first.

delivery-6-say.text: The signal is green now. Give me a final delivery report with the number of boxes, the destination, and the reason we waited.

delivery-6-hint.text: The five boxes are going to East Pier, and we waited because of the strong wind.

delivery-6-feedback.text: Delivery complete! You followed a schedule, asked for help, and adapted to a change. A fine job, harbor helper!

work-bake-rolls-order.text: Good morning, baker! The harbor crew has ordered six soft rolls. We will measure, mix, knead, shape, bake and pack them. Tell me what we are making.

work-bake-rolls-measure.text: First, measure 3 cups of flour, 1 cup of water, 1 spoonful of yeast, 1 spoonful of sugar, 1 spoonful of salt. Check each amount before you mix anything.

work-bake-mix.text: Now stir the ingredients four times. Move the spoon around the bowl until the dry flour disappears.

work-bake-knead.text: Next, fold and press the dough three times. Kneading makes the dough smooth and stretchy.

work-bake-rolls-shape.text: Shape the dough into 6 rolls. Make the pieces even so they bake together.

work-bake-rolls-oven.text: Set the oven to 180 degrees and the timer to 20 minutes. Check both settings before the tray goes in.

work-bake-oven.text: Put the tray in the oven. Our game oven bakes quickly. When the bread turns golden, take it out and let it cool.

work-bake-rolls-pack.text: The bread has cooled. Pack exactly 6 rolls for the customer. Count carefully before you finish.

work-bake-loaf-order.text: Our next order is one garden herb loaf for the cafe. This recipe uses more flour and fresh herbs. Listen carefully, then tell me which bread you will make.

work-bake-loaf-measure.text: First, measure 4 cups of flour, 2 cups of water, 1 spoonful of yeast, 1 spoonful of salt, 2 spoonfuls of herbs. Check each amount before you mix anything.

work-bake-loaf-shape.text: Shape the dough into 1 loaf. Make the pieces even so they bake together.

work-bake-loaf-oven.text: Set the oven to 200 degrees and the timer to 25 minutes. Check both settings before the tray goes in.

work-bake-loaf-pack.text: The bread has cooled. Pack exactly 1 loaf for the customer. Count carefully before you finish.

work-bake-braid-order.text: A family is coming for a picnic. They would like two sweet braided breads. We use milk instead of water, and a little more sugar. Please confirm the order.

work-bake-braid-measure.text: First, measure 3 cups of flour, 2 cups of milk, 1 spoonful of yeast, 2 spoonfuls of sugar, 1 spoonful of salt. Check each amount before you mix anything.

work-bake-braid-shape.text: Shape the dough into 2 braids. Make the pieces even so they bake together.

work-bake-braid-oven.text: Set the oven to 180 degrees and the timer to 25 minutes. Check both settings before the tray goes in.

work-bake-braid-pack.text: The bread has cooled. Pack exactly 2 braids for the customer. Count carefully before you finish.

work-guest-Alice-welcome.text: Hello! I have been exploring the harbor all morning. May I have a table for one near the window? A quiet seat would be lovely.

work-guest-Alice-order.text: I would like tomato soup with bread and water. Please leave out the cheese. Could you repeat my order so we can check it together?

work-service-prepare.text: Prepare the main dish, side, drink and special request. Read the ticket and check everything before you leave the kitchen.

work-service-table-2.text: The order belongs at table 2. Choose the matching table, then serve the meal politely.

work-guest-Alice-extra.text: The soup is delicious. I have spilled a little water. Could you bring me a clean napkin?

work-guest-Alice-bill.text: Thank you for looking after me. How much is my meal? Please tell me the total before I pay.

work-guest-Rowan-welcome.text: Good afternoon! I have finished a busy morning at the harbor. Is there a table where I can sit and have a warm meal?

work-guest-Rowan-order.text: Could I have grilled fish, a fresh salad and tea? Please do not put lemon on the fish. I would like to enjoy its own flavor.

work-service-table-1.text: The order belongs at table 1. Choose the matching table, then serve the meal politely.

work-guest-Rowan-extra.text: Everything looks wonderful. I have a spoon, but I need something for the salad. Could you bring me a fork?

work-guest-Rowan-bill.text: Thank you for looking after me. How much is my meal? Please tell me the total before I pay.

work-guest-Nora-welcome.text: Hello there! My granddaughter told me this restaurant has lovely vegetables. Could you help me find a comfortable table?

work-guest-Nora-order.text: I would like vegetable pasta, a side salad and fruit juice. Please make the pasta mild, not spicy. I want to taste all the vegetables.

work-service-table-3.text: The order belongs at table 3. Choose the matching table, then serve the meal politely.

work-guest-Nora-extra.text: This is a lovely meal. Could I also have water? There is no hurry; please bring it when you can.

work-guest-Nora-bill.text: Thank you for looking after me. How much is my meal? Please tell me the total before I pay.

work-guest-Hugo-welcome.text: Hello! We have been building sandcastles. I would love a light lunch before I join my family again. Is a table available?

work-guest-Hugo-order.text: May I have tomato soup, bread and lemonade? Please bring the bread without butter. I would like to keep it plain today.

work-guest-Hugo-extra.text: Thank you for remembering the plain bread. May I have another napkin before I finish?

work-guest-Hugo-bill.text: Thank you for looking after me. How much is my meal? Please tell me the total before I pay.

work-guest-Amira-welcome.text: Good afternoon! I work in the kitchen across the street. It is finally my lunch break. Could I sit somewhere sunny?

work-guest-Amira-order.text: I would like grilled fish, bread and water. Could you add extra lemon on the side? I like to squeeze it over the fish myself.

work-guest-Amira-extra.text: The fish is just right. I have finished my water. Could you refill my glass, please?

work-guest-Amira-bill.text: Thank you for looking after me. How much is my meal? Please tell me the total before I pay.

work-guest-Oliver-welcome.text: Hello! This is my first visit to Little Harbor. The museum guide recommended your restaurant. Could you show me to a table?

work-guest-Oliver-order.text: Please may I have vegetable pasta, salad and water? I do not want cheese on the pasta. Please keep the salad on a separate plate.

work-guest-Oliver-extra.text: The separate salad plate is helpful. Could I have a clean fork for the salad?

work-guest-Oliver-bill.text: Thank you for looking after me. How much is my meal? Please tell me the total before I pay.

work-clay-0-order.text: We are making a cup with ocean blue glaze and a waves pattern. Tell me the object and its color before we begin.

work-clay-3.text: Take 3 pieces of soft clay. Count the pieces so your object will have the right size.

work-clay-shape-Cup.text: Shape the clay into a cup. Use the picture in your plan to guide you.

work-clay-glaze-0.text: Brush on ocean blue glaze. This coating will make the pottery colorful after firing.

work-clay-pattern-Waves.text: Add the waves pattern. Keep the marks even and leave space between them.

work-clay-cool.text: The kiln is hot. Leave the pottery until it is completely cool. Which action is safe?

work-clay-1-order.text: We are making a bowl with leaf green glaze and a leaves pattern. Tell me the object and its color before we begin.

work-clay-5.text: Take 5 pieces of soft clay. Count the pieces so your object will have the right size.

work-clay-shape-Bowl.text: Shape the clay into a bowl. Use the picture in your plan to guide you.

work-clay-glaze-1.text: Brush on leaf green glaze. This coating will make the pottery colorful after firing.

work-clay-pattern-Leaves.text: Add the leaves pattern. Keep the marks even and leave space between them.

work-clay-2-order.text: We are making a vase with warm coral glaze and a dots pattern. Tell me the object and its color before we begin.

work-clay-4.text: Take 4 pieces of soft clay. Count the pieces so your object will have the right size.

work-clay-shape-Vase.text: Shape the clay into a vase. Use the picture in your plan to guide you.

work-clay-glaze-2.text: Brush on warm coral glaze. This coating will make the pottery colorful after firing.

work-clay-pattern-Dots.text: Add the dots pattern. Keep the marks even and leave space between them.

work-museum-welcome.text: Welcome, junior curator. We are preparing an exhibition about the sea and its history. Tell our visitors that you are ready to help them explore.

work-museum-fossil.text: This ancient shell has slowly turned into stone. It tells us about animals that lived long ago. Which display should it join?

work-museum-compass.text: A sailor used this compass to find north while crossing the sea. Choose the display about finding the way.

work-museum-sequence.text: Arrange these discoveries from oldest to newest: an ancient fossil, an old sailing compass, and a modern camera. Tap them in that order.

work-museum-guide.text: A visitor asks what a compass does. Explain its purpose in your own words. You can mention finding north or helping sailors choose a direction.

work-museum-label.text: The exhibit is ready. The fossil is delicate and easy to break. Which sign will help visitors care for it?

work-place-library-welcome.text: A storm scattered three books and the pages of a sea adventure. Help us rebuild the story. Tell me how you can help in the library.

work-place-library-shelves.text: A book called Ocean Animals belongs with nature. The Lost Compass is an adventure. Garden Soup contains recipes. Return each book to its correct shelf.

work-place-library-story.text: Milo found a map before he packed his bag. He packed before he sailed. Only after sailing did he discover the island. Put these events in order.

work-place-library-clue.text: Milo carries a compass because clouds hide the sun. What can you infer about the compass? Think about why it is useful when the sky is cloudy.

work-place-library-explain.text: A younger reader asks why Milo packed before sailing. Explain how planning helped him. Use the words before and prepared in your answer.

work-place-market-order.text: A customer has forty coins and wants two guppies and one tetra. They do not want a goldfish today. Repeat the order before you use the shopping basket.

work-place-market-basket.text: Guppies cost eight coins each, a tetra costs twelve, and a goldfish costs eighteen. Add exactly two guppies and one tetra. Watch the basket total and keep within forty coins.

work-place-market-change.text: Your basket costs twenty-eight coins. The customer pays with forty coins. Count the change carefully. How many coins should you return?

work-place-market-care.text: The customer asks whether more fish always make a better aquarium. Which reply explains the importance of space?

work-place-market-finish.text: Finish the sale politely. Tell the customer that the total is twenty-eight coins and the change is twelve coins. You may say the numbers or type them.

work-place-workshop-brief.text: Our customer wants a peaceful aquarium with a plant on the left, a cave in the middle, and a shell on the right. Confirm the three decorations before you design it.

work-place-workshop-layout.text: Use the bottom row of the design board. Place the plant at bottom left, the cave at bottom center, and the shell at bottom right. Leave the other six spaces empty for swimming.

work-place-workshop-tools.text: The customer wants to check the width of the cave before buying it. Choose the tool that measures length accurately.

work-place-workshop-process.text: A careful designer first measures the tank, then draws a plan, then places the decorations, and finally checks the swimming space. Put the work cards in that order.

work-place-workshop-explain.text: Show the customer your finished design. Explain where the cave is. Use between to describe its position in relation to the plant and shell.

work-place-harbor-order.text: A boat must carry two food crates and one medicine box. Its safe cargo limit is ten kilograms. Confirm the cargo before we prepare the loading plan.

work-place-harbor-cargo.text: Each food crate weighs three kilograms. A medicine box weighs two, and a tool chest weighs five. Load two food crates and one medicine box. Stay within the ten-kilogram limit.

work-place-harbor-route.text: The boat starts at the bottom-left dock. Rocks block the middle channel. Go north twice, then east three times to reach the lighthouse dock. Follow each direction carefully.

work-place-harbor-depart.text: Before departure, check the weather, count the cargo, close the cargo hatch, and then untie the boat. Arrange the safety checklist in order.

work-place-harbor-report.text: Tell Captain Finn that the cargo weighs eight kilograms and the boat is ready. Include the weight and the word ready in your report.

work-place-aquarium-help.text: Welcome to the aquarium care lab. This is a pretend tank for learning. Today we will check the water, feed the fish carefully, and keep their home clean. Tell me you are ready to help.

work-place-aquarium-controls.text: Read our game care card: this pretend tank needs a temperature of twenty-four degrees and a filter level of three. Move both controls to match the care card.

work-place-aquarium-food.text: There is leftover food at the bottom of the tank. More food would make the water dirty. What should the keeper do next?

work-place-aquarium-clean.text: Put the care routine in order: observe the fish, check the water, remove leftover food, and then record your observations.

work-place-aquarium-report.text: Explain one reason to keep the water clean. You can say that clean water helps the fish stay healthy. Use clean water and healthy in your reply.

work-place-cafe-order.text: A visitor wants a warm honey tea with lemon. They would like one spoonful of honey and no milk. Repeat the important parts of the drink order.

work-place-cafe-layers.text: First place the tea bag in the cup. Next add warm water. Then stir in honey, and add lemon last. Build the drink in the same order.

work-place-cafe-tray.text: Prepare the takeaway tray with one tea and two biscuits. Tea costs five coins and each biscuit costs two. The visitor has ten coins. Keep the tray within the budget.

work-place-cafe-total.text: The tea costs five coins and the two biscuits cost four coins altogether. What is the total price of this takeaway order?

work-place-cafe-deliver.text: Hand over the order politely. Tell the visitor that the tea is warm and ask them to carry it carefully.

work-place-garden-plan.text: We are planting a small garden. We need a rose on the left and a sunflower on the right. Tell me which two flowers you will plant.

work-place-garden-plant.text: Use the bottom row of the garden bed. Plant a rose in the bottom-left patch and a sunflower in the bottom-right patch. Leave the center empty as a little path.

work-place-garden-care.text: For this game, our care card asks for two cups of water and six hours of sunlight. Adjust the two controls to match the card. Too much water is not always helpful.

work-place-garden-weather.text: Rain is coming this afternoon and the soil is already wet. What is the most thoughtful choice for the garden?

work-place-garden-explain.text: Tell a visitor how sunlight helps your garden. Use flowers, sunlight and grow in one clear sentence.

work-place-lighthouse-watch.text: The harbor fog is thick tonight. We will use colored signals to guide a boat safely home. Tell me that you are ready to watch the light and help the boat.

work-place-lighthouse-code.text: Our harbor code is simple: red means stop, green means proceed, and yellow means wait. Match the three lights to their meanings before you send a signal.

work-place-lighthouse-flash.text: The captain asks for this signal: yellow, yellow, green. Listen or watch the demonstration, then press the colored pads in the same order. You can replay it as often as you need.

work-place-lighthouse-guide.text: Guide the rescue boat around the rocks. From the bottom-left dock, travel north twice and east three times. The lighthouse marks the safe destination.

work-place-lighthouse-report.text: Explain your signal to the captain. Tell him that yellow means wait and green means proceed.

work-place-studio-brief.text: We are painting a tiny harbor picture from spoken instructions. The sky will be blue, the sun yellow, and the water green. Repeat the three colors before you pick up your brush.

work-place-studio-paint.text: Paint all three squares in the top row blue. Paint the center square yellow. Paint all three squares in the bottom row green. Leave the two remaining squares empty.

work-place-studio-mix.text: The artist mixes blue paint with yellow paint to make the water color. Which color should appear?

work-place-studio-process.text: Before a gallery opens, an artist sketches the idea, paints the picture, lets it dry, and finally adds a title. Arrange those steps.

work-place-studio-present.text: Describe your picture to a visitor. Explain that the yellow sun is above the green water. Use above in your sentence.

work-place-post-welcome.text: Three letters need delivering. One goes to the library, one to the bakery, and one to the inn. Tell me the three destinations before we sort the mail.

work-place-post-sort.text: Lily works at the library on Book Lane. Oliver works at the bakery on Rose Street. Mrs. Reed manages the inn on Sea Road. Match each addressed envelope to its destination.

work-place-post-priority.text: The bakery closes first, the library closes next, and the inn stays open late. Deliver the bakery letter first, the library letter second, and the inn letter last.

work-place-post-damaged.text: A parcel has a torn address label and you cannot read the house number. Which action will help it reach the correct person?

work-place-post-finish.text: Tell the postmaster your route using first and then. Explain that you will visit the bakery first and the library next.

work-place-music-welcome.text: Welcome to the harbor sound studio. We will listen to a short melody, copy it, and get ready for a performance. Tell me that you are ready to listen and play.

work-place-music-notes.text: Our first melody is do, mi, so. Listen to the three notes, then press the matching pads in order. You can replay the melody and take as much time as you need.

work-place-music-memory.text: Now try a longer phrase: so, mi, re, do. Listen carefully for the melody moving down. Copy all four notes in order.

work-place-music-show.text: A considerate performer listens to the count-in, plays the melody, lets the final note finish, and then bows. Put the performance cards in order.

work-place-music-finish.text: Describe the longer melody. It starts high and ends low. Use high and low to explain what you heard.

work-place-inn-welcome.text: Two travelers need rooms. A family needs two beds on the ground floor. A writer needs a quiet upstairs room away from music. Welcome them and offer to help find suitable rooms.

work-place-inn-rooms.text: Room one has two beds on the ground floor. Room two is upstairs beside the music room. Room three is a quiet upstairs room facing the garden. Match the family and the writer to suitable rooms.

work-place-inn-price.text: The family room costs thirty coins per night. The family is staying for two nights. What is the room charge before any extras?

work-place-inn-requests.text: The family asks for an extra towel. The writer asks for a desk lamp. Send each item to the correct room and check the request before delivery.

work-place-inn-directions.text: Explain to the writer that room three is upstairs and faces the garden. Include the room number, upstairs and garden in your directions.
